title.official: AI Impact Summit Declaration, New Delhi
title.short: New Delhi Declaration on AI Impact

issuer.name: Government of India, Ministry of External Affairs, and participating States and international organisations

relevance.reason: The declaration adopted at the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi on 19 February 2026, the fourth summit in the series that began at Bletchley Park in 2023. The Press Information Bureau's annex lists 92 endorsers as of 5 March 2026: 90 States, the European Union and IFAD, the widest endorsement count among the summit declarations in the corpus. It marks the series' shift from AI safety to AI impact and development, and it is a political declaration, not a treaty: it creates no legal obligation, ratification, depositary, monitoring or dispute settlement. It is included because the corpus already catalogues the Bletchley, Seoul and Paris summit texts and would otherwise omit the 2026 stage of the same series.
ai_provisions: Preamble — AI's promise is best realised when its benefits are shared by humanity; the participants adopt the principle 'Sarvajan Hitaya, Sarvajan Sukhaya' (welfare for all, happiness for all).

Seven pillars (Chakras) — democratising AI resources; economic growth and social good; secure and trusted AI; AI for science; access for social empowerment; human capital development; resilient, efficient and innovative AI systems.
Democratising AI resources — robust digital infrastructure and affordable access, with international cooperation on compute, data, models and skills.
Secure and trusted AI — trustworthy frameworks, risk management and respect for national sovereignty.
AI for science and for social empowerment — use of AI in research and public services, including for development priorities.
Human capital development — skilling and reskilling, including the Equitable AI Transitions Playbook produced with the International Labour Organization.
Complementarity with existing international initiatives — the declaration is to be read alongside, not instead of, other international and regional AI processes.
relevance.excluded_scope: A political declaration. It creates no binding obligation, no signature or ratification, no depositary, no monitoring or reporting duty and no dispute-settlement mechanism. The separate New Delhi Frontier AI Impact Commitments, announced by 13 model providers at the same summit, are a different instrument and are not counted as parties to the declaration. National implementation is not assessed.

dates.notes: Adopted at the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi on 19 February 2026; the summit ran from 18 to 19 February 2026. The Press Information Bureau's annex states that the list is 'as of 5th March 2026' and names 92 endorsers; the Ministry of External Affairs page was last updated on 21 February 2026 and lists 91, without Colombia. The text has no signature, ratification, depositary or entry-into-force clause.

status_note: Non-binding political declaration, not a treaty. The Press Information Bureau's annex lists 92 endorsers as of 5 March 2026: 90 States, the European Union and IFAD. The Ministry of External Affairs page updated 21 February 2026 lists 91 and omits Colombia. The record uses the later PIB list and records the discrepancy; it does not infer any other missing endorsement. The declaration creates no legal obligation, ratification, depositary, monitoring or dispute settlement. The separate New Delhi Frontier AI Impact Commitments were announced by 13 model providers and are not part of this declaration.

related.note: The previous stage of the same summit series: Paris 2025 was an 'AI Action Summit'; New Delhi 2026 was an 'AI Impact Summit'. Both are non-binding political declarations.
The first summit of the series, focused on frontier-model safety; New Delhi marks the series' shift toward impact, development and access.
The second summit of the series; Seoul combined safety and innovation themes.

WAICO was signed five months after the New Delhi Declaration and also addresses AI capacity building in the Global South, but it is a treaty establishing an intergovernmental organization, not a summit declaration.
The Global Digital Compact in the Pact for the Future is the UN's universal digital-cooperation framework; the New Delhi Declaration is a separate, non-binding summit text.

provenance.discovered_via: Search for the outcome of the 2026 AI Impact Summit while auditing the summit series against the corpus. The declaration was missing from the 42-record corpus; the official MEA text and the PIB release were then read. The PIB annex was subsequently found to contain the full 92-name list, correcting an earlier record that said no itemised list existed.
